intro: Requires the AI gateway environment on mesh1. Azure and Bedrock are local model simulators; Anthropic is a live provider and needs a valid key. Model calls to Anthropic incur usage charges. Reset removes this lab's routes and policies and restores the local primary provider.

1.title: Route corporate model names
1.say: Map application-facing model names to provider backends and test each mapping.
1.point: The response identifies the serving model. Azure and Bedrock are simulated locally; Anthropic is live.

blocks.title: One backend per provider
blocks.instruction: Apply the Azure, Bedrock and Anthropic backend definitions. The Anthropic backend uses a Secret and model aliases.
blocks.show:
kind: EnterpriseAgentgatewayBackend
  azure-gpt5        gpt-5-nano
  bedrock-haiku     claude-haiku-4-5
  anthropic-claude  premium-reasoning
                    -> claude-sonnet-4-5

blocks.title: Route on the model in the body
blocks.instruction: Extract the requested model into x-model-name before routing. Match that header in the HTTPRoute.
blocks.expect: extract-model and the models route are applied.
blocks.show:
phase: PreRouting
  set x-model-name: json(request.body).model
kind: HTTPRoute   # match x-model-name -> backend

blocks.title: Ask for each name
blocks.instruction: Send one request for each corporate name and one unknown name.
blocks.expect: Named models reach their configured backends. The unknown name uses the Azure simulator default.
blocks.show:
for M in corporate-fast corporate-secure premium-reasoning \
         corporate-premium anything-else; do
  curl $GATEWAY/models/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"'$M'"...}'

2.title: Test provider failover
2.say: Configure a primary provider and a fallback group. Stop the primary and inspect the results.
2.point: A failed request triggers eviction. Subsequent requests can use the fallback group until the primary is eligible again.

blocks.title: Priority groups and a health policy

parts.title: Configure provider priorities
parts.instruction: Apply the resilient backend, its route and a health policy that evicts a provider for 60 seconds after a 5xx or 429.
parts.expect: The backend, route and health policy are applied.

parts.title: Check the healthy primary
parts.instruction: Send a request before stopping the primary provider.
parts.expect: The Azure simulator answers as gpt-5-nano.

blocks.show:
ai.groups:
  - primary            (Azure)
  - fallback-bedrock, fallback-anthropic
health: response.code >= 500 -> evict 60s

blocks.title: Take Azure down

parts.title: Stop the primary provider
parts.instruction: Scale the local Azure simulator to zero.

parts.title: Test fallback requests
parts.instruction: Send eight requests to the same resilient endpoint.
parts.expect: After the primary fails, the fallback group serves requests.

blocks.show:
kubectl -n ai-models scale deploy/azure-openai --replicas=0
8 x POST /resilient/v1/chat/completions

blocks.title: Inspect requests by model
blocks.instruction: Read the gateway's request counters for the resilient route.
blocks.expect: The metrics include models from the fallback group. A small sample may not use both providers.
blocks.show:
curl localhost:15020/metrics \
  | sum token_usage_count by gen_ai_response_model

blocks.title: Bring Azure back
blocks.instruction: Restore the primary simulator and restart the gateway to clear its eviction state.
blocks.show:
kubectl -n ai-models scale deploy/azure-openai --replicas=1
kubectl -n $NS rollout restart deploy/ai-gateway

3.title: Require user identity
3.say: Require a signed token on the models route and add identity claims to model metrics.
3.point: Anonymous requests return 401. Alice's valid token allows the request and supplies metric attributes.

blocks.title: JWT and identity on metrics
blocks.instruction: Configure the demo issuer's public keys and metric attributes for user, team and business unit.
blocks.show:
jwtAuthentication: { mode: Strict }   # issuer idp.demo.example
metrics.attributes:
  user: jwt.sub   team: jwt.team   business_unit: jwt.businessUnit

blocks.title: With and without a token
blocks.instruction: Send an anonymous request, then repeat it with alice's token.
blocks.expect: The anonymous request returns 401 and alice returns 200.

4.title: Restrict premium models by group
4.say: Premium models are for engineering. One CEL rule reads the model from the body and the groups from the JWT.
4.point: bob from finance gets 403 on premium and 200 on a standard model. alice from engineering gets premium.

parts.title: Apply the model access rule
parts.instruction: Allow premium model names only when the token includes the engineering group.

parts.title: Compare engineering and finance
parts.instruction: Request premium models as bob and alice, then request a standard model as bob.
parts.expect: Bob is denied premium access but can use standard models. Alice can use premium models.

checks.label: bob, standard: 200
checks.match: bob asks for a standard model:\s+HTTP 200

5.title: Limit token usage per user
5.say: Use the JWT subject as the key for a per-user token allowance.
5.point: Bob's requests exhaust his allowance. Alice has a separate allowance and can still make a request.

blocks.title: 60 tokens a minute per user

parts.title: Set the token allowance
parts.instruction: Configure 60 tokens per minute per user and attach the limit to the models route.
parts.expect: The rate limit configuration and policy are applied.

parts.title: Test independent user limits
parts.instruction: Send requests as bob, a few seconds apart, until he is limited. Then send one as alice.
parts.expect: Bob receives 429 after exhausting his allowance. Alice receives 200.

blocks.show:
kind: RateLimitConfig
  key: user = jwt.sub   type: TOKEN
  requestsPerUnit: 60   unit: MINUTE

blocks.title: Restore the larger allowance
blocks.instruction: Set the allowance to 500,000 tokens per day for the remaining chapters.

6.title: Give a service a key and budget
6.say: Create a virtual key for a CI job, attach a daily budget and test enforcement.
6.point: An invalid key returns 401. The valid key is allowed until the budget is exhausted, then receives 429.

blocks.title: Mint a key, set a budget

parts.title: Create the virtual key and route
parts.instruction: Create a fresh virtual key in a labelled Secret and a route to the local model simulator.
parts.expect: The Secret, backend and service-models route are applied.

parts.title: Set the key's budget
parts.instruction: Read the key ID from the Secret. Attach a 100-token daily budget and strict key authentication.
parts.expect: The budget and authentication policy are applied.

parts.title: Test authentication and the budget
parts.instruction: Try an invalid key, then use the virtual key until its allowance is spent.
parts.expect: The invalid key returns 401. The valid key starts at 200, then receives 429.

blocks.show:
kind: Secret   # virtual-key-set: llm-consumers
kind: EnterpriseAgentgatewayBudget
  virtualKey: $VKID
  limit: 100 Tokens / Day
  onBudgetExceeded: Block

checks.label: Blocked once the budget is spent

blocks.title: Inspect budget enforcement
blocks.instruction: Read the budget status, generated rate limit configuration and gateway denial log.
blocks.expect: The budget is accepted and enforced. The gateway logs over_limit_block.
blocks.show:
kubectl get enterpriseagentgatewaybudgets
kubectl get ratelimitconfigs
kubectl logs deploy/ai-gateway | grep budget

7.title: Attribute model usage and cost
7.say: Generate requests from three users and inspect usage grouped by their identity claims.
7.point: The metrics show token counts and catalogue-based costs. Costs for simulated providers are illustrative, not provider invoices.

blocks.title: Traffic from three users
blocks.instruction: Send seven model requests using alice, bob and carol's tokens.
blocks.show:
alice: premium-reasoning, corporate-fast, corporate-secure, corporate-premium
bob:   anything-else
carol: corporate-secure, premium-reasoning

blocks.title: Sum the proxy's metrics
blocks.instruction: Group the gateway counters by business unit, team, user and model.
blocks.expect: The counters include the three users' claims and the model catalogue lookup status.
blocks.show:
sum token_usage by business_unit
sum token_usage by team
sum cost_usd    by user, model

8.title: Control MCP tool access
8.say: Expose an MCP server and use JWT groups to restrict one of its tools.
8.point: bob never sees printenv, and calling it anyway is refused. alice sees and calls it.

blocks.title: Put the MCP server behind the gateway

parts.title: Expose the MCP backend
parts.instruction: Apply the MCP backend and its /mcp route.
parts.expect: mcp-hub and the mcp HTTPRoute are applied.

parts.title: List the available tools
parts.instruction: List tools through the gateway before adding authentication.
parts.expect: The list includes echo, sum and printenv.

blocks.show:
kind: EnterpriseAgentgatewayBackend
  entMcp.targets: everything  (StreamableHTTP)
kind: HTTPRoute   /mcp

blocks.title: JWT and per-tool authorisation

parts.title: Apply authentication and tool permissions
parts.instruction: Require the demo JWT and restrict printenv to the engineering group.
parts.expect: The JWT and tool authorisation policies are applied.

parts.title: Compare tool discovery
parts.instruction: List tools as bob and alice, then attempt anonymous initialisation.
parts.expect: Only alice sees printenv. Anonymous initialisation returns 401.

blocks.show:
jwtAuthentication: { mode: Strict }
mcp.authorization:
  'mcp.tool.name != "printenv"
   || jwt.groups.exists(g, g == "engineering")'

blocks.title: Call the tools
blocks.instruction: Call sum as bob, then attempt printenv as bob and alice.
blocks.expect: Bob can call sum but not printenv. Alice can call printenv.
blocks.show:
mcp_call "$BOB"   sum      '{"a":2,"b":3}'
mcp_call "$BOB"   printenv '{}'
mcp_call "$ALICE" printenv '{}'

where-this-goes-next.title: Review the results and reset
where-this-goes-next.say: Inspect the traffic in Solo UI, Tracing or Cost Management, then reset the lab.
where-this-goes-next.point: Open Solo UI, Tracing or Cost to see the same traffic from the platform side.
